answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a jade as the anchor of the cost.
